title: Power Apps: header and navigation refresh for model-driven apps
summary: The briefing's rollout facts, opt-in behaviour, licensing and maker control are supported. The maker path should include environment selection; the cited pages opened successfully during this check.

claims.claim: The refresh redesigns the model-driven app header.
claims.quote: It builds on the New Look (wave 1) with a redesigned app header, streamlined sitemap, and reworked form layout that gives users more space to focus on their work.

claims.claim: The refresh streamlines the sitemap.
claims.quote: Modern app header and streamlined sitemap: Updated styling aligned to the Fluent design system with a simplified sitemap that reduces navigation complexity.

claims.claim: The refresh reworks form layout.
claims.quote: It builds on the New Look (wave 1) with a redesigned app header, streamlined sitemap, and reworked form layout that gives users more space to focus on their work.

claims.claim: Learn calls the refresh wave 2, building on the New Look wave 1.
claims.quote: The header and navigation refresh (wave 2) is the next step in modernizing model-driven apps. It builds on the New Look (wave 1)

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The feature documentation describes no new data access or movement for this layout and navigation refresh.
claims.quote: Searched: "header and navigation refresh" mandatory permissions data access automatic admin switch. Opened modern-fluent-design in full and read the roadmap description; neither describes new data access or movement.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap nor the feature's Learn page describes new permissions, roles or sign-in behaviour for this refresh.
claims.quote: Searched: "header and navigation refresh" mandatory permissions data access automatic admin switch. Read modern-fluent-design and the roadmap in full; neither specifies new permissions, roles or sign-in behaviour for the refresh.

claims.claim: No autonomous behaviour is described; the feature page's automatic refresh behaviour concerns Plan designer apps.
claims.quote: Searched: "header and navigation refresh" mandatory permissions data access automatic admin switch. Read modern-fluent-design in full: it documents automatic application to Plan designer apps and no autonomous actions for the refresh.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The refresh is an included option in model-driven apps, whose users need a licence providing Power Apps premium use rights.
claims.quote: Every user who runs a model-driven app needs a license that provides Power Apps premium use rights.

claims.claim: The licensing FAQ says model-driven apps use Dataverse and are premium apps by default.
claims.quote: Model-driven apps use Dataverse and are premium apps by default.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published an additional licence requirement specific to the header and navigation refresh.
claims.quote: Searched: "header and navigation refresh" license pricing meter premium. Opened modern-fluent-design and powerapps-licensing-faq; no refresh-specific additional licence requirement was stated.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a meter specific to the header and navigation refresh.
claims.quote: Searched: "header and navigation refresh" license pricing meter premium. Read modern-fluent-design, powerapps-licensing-faq and returned pay-as-you-go-meters excerpts; no separate refresh meter was documented.

claims.claim: The feature's Learn page lists no licence or charge for the refresh.
claims.quote: Searched: "header and navigation refresh" license pricing meter premium. Opened modern-fluent-design in full; its wave 2 description, enablement steps and FAQ name no licence or charge for the refresh.

claims.claim: The mail app supports the modern, refreshed look, with its own enablement details on the Learn page.
claims.quote: The mail app supports the modern, refreshed look. It's on by default for environments on the monthly channel as part of the February 2026 release, and will be enabled on the semi-annual channel with the October 2026 update.

claims.claim: The mobile app supports the modern, refreshed look, with separate enablement guidance.
claims.quote: The mobile app also supports the modern, refreshed look. Admins can enable it by adding the Mobile modern experience setting to a solution and updating the value for the environment or for individual apps (2 = on).

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The maker path is Solutions > solution > Apps > app > Edit > Settings > Features > Header and navigation refresh.
claims.quote: In the app designer, select Settings on the command bar. Select Features, and then enable Header and navigation refresh.
claims.fix: Use 'environment > Solutions > solution > Apps > app > Edit > Settings > Features > Header and navigation refresh' in the control and rollout instructions. The cited https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/model-driven-apps/create-edit-app documents environment selection before Solutions and the remaining entry steps.

claims.claim: Makers save and publish the app after changing its settings.
claims.quote: You must select Publish to activate an app settings change. ... Save and Publish the app.

claims.claim: A documented automation call specifically setting the header and navigation refresh has not been established.
claims.quote: Searched: "header and navigation refresh" with SaveSettingValue, API, Power Platform CLI, PowerShell and Dataverse table entity reference. Opened SaveSettingValue, client API and feature pages; no refresh-specific call or setting name.

claims.claim: SaveSettingValue is a generic action creating or updating an app or organisation-level setting override.
claims.quote: Creates or updates app/organization level override.

claims.claim: Learn does not state the unique name of the header and navigation refresh setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "header and navigation refresh" "setting" "unique"; also Dataverse table entity reference API. Opened modern-fluent-design, app-properties, SaveSettingValue and client API guidance; no refresh setting unique name was stated.

claims.where: Governance controls; Open questions; front matter: defaultState
claims.claim: Learn documents no environment-wide or tenant-wide admin switch specifically for this refresh.
claims.quote: Searched: "header and navigation refresh" with environment, switch, SaveSettingValue, API, tenant, Power Platform CLI and PowerShell. Read modern-fluent-design, app-properties and generic setting API pages; no refresh-wide admin switch found.

claims.claim: Learn documents a separate New look for model driven apps setting that can be added to a solution.
claims.quote: Select Add Existing > More > Setting. ... Select New look for model driven apps. ... Select Add to add it to the solution.

claims.claim: The feature page retains revert instructions saying admins can turn off the New Look, which the briefing flags as conflicting guidance.
claims.quote: Admins can turn off the New Look for all users by updating the New look for model driven apps app setting.

claims.claim: The app settings page says the New Look setting is hidden and ignored from 2026 Wave 1, when the New Look becomes mandatory.
claims.quote: This setting is hidden and ignored with the 2026 Wave 1 release when the new look becomes mandatory.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated a date for making wave 2 mandatory; its feature page says it remains opt-in.
claims.quote: Searched: "header and navigation refresh" mandatory permissions data access automatic admin switch. Read modern-fluent-design: wave 2 is opt-in today, and the April 2026 New Look mandate explicitly does not include wave 2; no wave 2 mandate date is given.

claims.claim: The roadmap's Applies to field names model-driven apps.
claims.quote:
Applies to
Model-driven apps
